09003.story: As of Oct 6, cash rent in Hartford County runs $152 an acre for 2026, the highest of 6 in Connecticut and well over the state median of $83. That rent is up 33.3% from $114 in 2016. The census value of land and buildings came in at $15,160 an acre in 2022, 3rd highest of 8, though it slipped 6.0% from $16,126 in 2017. 27% of the farmland was rented in 2022.

09005.story: As of Oct 6, cash rent in Litchfield County runs $47 an acre for 2025, up 42.4% from $33 in 2014. The census value of land and buildings came in at $14,512 an acre in 2022, up 28.2% from $11,322 in 2017, or 5.1% a year. That puts the county 4th highest of 8 in Connecticut, a little over the state median of $13,767.

09007.story: As of Oct 12, cash rent in Middlesex County runs $68 an acre for 2026, 2nd lowest of 6 in Connecticut against a state median of $83. The census value of land and buildings was $15,325 an acre in 2022, up 2.8% from $14,911 in 2017, 0.5% a year. That value sits 2nd highest of 8 in the state, well over the $13,767 state median. 26% of the county's farmland was rented in 2022.

09009.story: As of Oct 6, cash rent in New Haven County runs $80 an acre in 2026, a little under the state median of $83 and 3rd lowest of 6. The census value of land and buildings is another story at $25,431 an acre in 2022, highest of 8 in Connecticut and well over the $13,767 state median. That figure was $23,490 in 2017, up 8.3% or 1.6% a year. 37% of the farmland was rented in 2022.

09011.story: As of Oct 6, cash rent in New London County runs $86 an acre for 2026, up 77.3% from $49 in 2016. That puts it 3rd highest of 6 in the state, a little over the $83 state median. The census value of land and buildings came to $12,043 an acre in 2022, up 5.0% from 2017, or 1.0% a year, and it sits 3rd lowest of 8. Only 18% of farmland here was rented in 2022.

09013.story: As of Oct 6, cash rent in Tolland County runs $90 an acre for 2026, up 8.4% from $83 in 2016 and 2nd highest of 6 in Connecticut. The census value of land and buildings came in at $13,021 an acre in 2022, up 34.2% from $9,703 in 2017. That still sits 4th lowest of 8 in the state, under the $13,767 state median. 25% of farmland here was rented in 2022.

09015.story: As of Oct 12, cash rent in Windham County runs $56 an acre in 2026, up 30.2% from $43 in 2016. That is the lowest of 6 in Connecticut, against a state median of $83. The census value of land and buildings came to $10,546 an acre in 2022, up 11.6% from $9,452 in 2017, and it is the lowest of 8 against a state median of $13,767. In 2022, 19% of the farmland was rented.
